headline: A well received 30 year Treasury auction and Trump's pledge not to strike Iran before the November 3 midterms pulled long end yields and crude lower on Friday, lifting US and Indian equities alongside gold, silver and copper in the same session.

summary.us: The S&P 500 closed at 7,811.54 up 0.59 percent and the Nasdaq Composite at 27,366.17 up 0.64 percent, with the Dow adding 423 points to 51,655, as a tech rebound and cheaper crude reversed Thursday's selloff that followed a Financial Times report putting OpenAI annualized revenue near 50 billion dollars, about 20 billion below the figure investors had been shown. Demand at Wednesday's 22 billion dollar 30 year auction, which cleared at 5.618 percent with a 2.54 bid to cover, cooled long end yields and left the 10 year near 5.24 percent ahead of September CPI on Oct 14 and the FOMC meeting on Oct 27 and 28.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 closed at 22,520.45 up 1.3 percent and the Sensex rebounded 879 points to 72,472, snapping a two day slide, with the Nifty IT index up more than 3 percent after TCS reported September quarter profit of 13,884 crore rupees, a 15 percent rise, following Thursday's close. Foreign investors stayed net sellers at about 3,569 crore rupees in the cash segment while domestic institutions bought about 4,743 crore, and the rupee held near 96.78 a dollar after the RBI raised the repo rate 25 basis points to 5.50 percent on Oct 7, its first hike since February 2023.
summary.global: Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose 1.79 percent to 24,211 and the Nikkei 225 ended flat at 69,031, while Korean markets were shut for a public holiday after the KOSPI fell 2.62 percent on Thursday as Samsung shares slipped despite a quarterly profit above 100 trillion won. European equities advanced, with the FTSE 100 up 1.06 percent and the DAX up 1.13 percent, and the dollar index was little changed at 102.23 as the euro held near 1.1231 and ECB hike expectations cooled.

weekly.narrative: The week turned on the long end of the Treasury curve, where yields pushed to multi year highs midweek and the 30 year auction cleared at 5.618 percent, the highest since August 2000, before solid demand cooled the move and let the S&P 500 finish 1.15 percent higher and the Nasdaq 0.64 percent higher despite a Thursday air pocket when the Financial Times reported OpenAI annualized revenue about 20 billion dollars below the figure circulated to investors. India spent the week absorbing the RBI's first rate hike since February 2023, a 25 basis point move to 5.50 percent on Oct 7 paired with a hawkish calibrated tightening stance and an FY27 CPI forecast lifted to 5.2 percent, which left the Nifty up only 0.44 percent while Bank Nifty gained 1.48 percent and foreign investors kept selling, including a 12,944 crore rupee outflow on Oct 8. Metals were the cleanest trade, with copper up 3.37 percent on the Centinela strike in Chile and Chinese restocking, and silver and gold adding 1.89 and 1.39 percent as real yields retreated into Friday. Crypto went the other way, bitcoin down 2.58 percent and ether down 7.34 percent on the week, pressured by high oil costs, rate hike expectations and Middle East risk. Next week brings the first real test of earnings season, with JPMorgan and Citigroup on Oct 13 and Bank of America on Oct 14, alongside US September CPI on Oct 14 that the street expects at 3.6 percent on the year, India September CPI, and TSMC results on Oct 15.
